chunk_map.heading: Would you let an agent post your weekly update?

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 0 line 6: "It does not work for every agent a team runs." closest; 'It' resolves to 'Reading every draft yourself' in the preceding sentence; 'the answers' (l.8) resolves to the three questions in l.6; header and l.4 name 'the team's weekly update' before 'every draft'.
grep for 'opening lecture|earlier lecture|the lecture|prework' in body -> none; l.4-8 name no other file or position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no 'the X you did/saw/caught' backward reference in body (l.4-8)

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess-before-reveal or demo beat; l.4-8 are verbed sentences

rules_evaluated.evidence: l.4-8: three paragraphs; closest to thin is l.4 'Take the team's weekly update...People act on it.' but it sets the scene the slide builds on; the slide as a whole carries the claim 'choosing which, for which work, is the job'.
l.1 'Would you let an agent post your weekly update?' vs l.8 four answers from draft only to never without a person; the body answers the question it asks, no contradiction.

closest: l.6 'What can the agent reach? Which check runs every time? Where does a person still belong?' three questions, but each opens differently and carries a distinct design choice (reach, check, person), so not anaphora; no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' (grep 'Not ' -> 0 in body), no self-grading superlative, no number+retraction, no empty-leg verb triplet; l.8 four-item list is a semicolon enumeration of distinct answers.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest: l.6 'designing the loop'; 'loop' is spine vocabulary an engineer in the room uses, not repo dialect; grep surface|firing|compendium|forcing function|beat|mood -> 0 in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget - bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c '\*\*' body.txt -> 0; no bold, within the <=1 budget.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content - verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no renderer/section-wrapper change; single standalone slide file with one ## chunk, nothing phase-less

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering - position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/slides/one-level-up.md -> 'OK - 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent.' exit 0; header carries no hand number.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/slides/one-level-up.md -> 'OK - 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.' exit 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no links in body (grep -c '](' body.txt -> 0); review surface, never a gate

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size - 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/slides/one-level-up.md -> 'oversized: 0', exit 0; limits 210 words / 6 bullets.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: l.1 '## Would you let an agent post your weekly update?' is a lecture-slide header posing the question the body answers; not an exercise imperative-or-phase header, and not a law/consolidation slide where a claim is required; an orientation-style question header is not a violation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies - three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest: l.8 'Choosing which, for which work, is the job.' reads as a kicker, but it names the move (pick the answer per kind of work) that the preceding list sets up rather than restating the header; no doctrine restatement, no design commentary.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: header l.1 promises a decision on letting an agent post; every paragraph (l.4 scene, l.6 move up a level, l.8 four answers) answers it; maintainer STATUS says the slide was rewritten whole, no inherited old-header bullets remain.

notes: One accept-note in maintainer block (STATUS 2026-10-06 rewrite); none covers a passage a rule catches. Simulation training, not taught.
